PATitle: Trainer guide: monitoring alert identification and practice handoff
PASubtitle: A fictional, read-only datacenter monitoring simulation
TargetAudience: New datacenter monitoring staff in the fictional scenario; delivered by a trainer.
ActivityDescription: Teach participants to turn a displayed monitoring observation into a factual handoff, without inferring a cause or changing a status. The assessment identifies the skill gap; the fictional SOP supplies the record, responsibilities, materials, and boundaries. This guide adds a trainer-led teaching sequence and individual practice, not a technical response procedure.
TrainerGuidelines:
Before practice, explain the simulation-only boundaries in Notes. Stop if real systems, operational details, or out-of-scope actions are introduced.
Demonstrate with SIM-042: read the five displayed details, distinguish the observation from the unverified cause, and address a fictional handoff to Practice Review Lead. Explain that receipt is not resolution.
Ask participants why an observation does not establish a cause. Keep the displayed Needs review status unchanged.
Observe each participant during a normal handoff and a destination-withheld attempt. Give feedback against Validation and request another attempt for any missed criterion.
DesiredLearningOutcome: Participants can identify the fictional monitoring record details and communicate a factual practice handoff to the designated role, while recognizing unsupported assumptions and staying within read-only simulation boundaries.
WhatIsNeeded:
Prepare a printed or locally displayed copy of SIM-042: 09:15 exercise time; Observe Queue; Needs review; a placeholder monitoring update has not appeared on the practice display; cause unverified.
Prepare a Practice Review Lead role card, blank handoff cards, and pencils or a local text editor.
Prepare another attempt with the destination card withheld so participants can practise pausing and asking the trainer.
No accounts, credentials, external messaging, or infrastructure connections are needed. Session duration is not supplied; agree it before scheduling.
SkillsBasedLearningObjectives:
Identify the record identifier, displayed timestamp, monitoring label, displayed status, and observation accurately.
Distinguish an observation from an inferred cause and name the designated practice review role.
Communicate a complete factual handoff, leave the status unchanged, and pause for clarification when the destination is absent.
DocumentationAndReferences:
Fictional training-needs assessment: A1 Audience and skill gap; A2 Required competencies; A3 Observable success requirements.
Fictional SOP: S1 Read-only monitoring record; S2 Responsibilities and handoff; S3 Materials and preparation; S4 Operating boundaries.
Both sources are newly authored public fixtures in monitoring-sources.json, not internal documents. Source connections in the browser are manually curated teaching aids, not model-generated citations.
ActivitySteps:
Trainer briefing: explain the skill gap and the simulation-only boundaries before distributing the fictional materials.
Trainer demonstration: read SIM-042 aloud, identify its five displayed details, distinguish observation from cause, and demonstrate a handoff to Practice Review Lead without changing Needs review.
Learner practice: each participant reads the same record and prepares a handoff with all five details, the designated review role, and an explicit unverified-cause statement.
Exception practice: withhold the destination card. Each participant pauses and asks the trainer rather than inventing a recipient or sending anything.
Trainer check and feedback: observe each participant against Validation, request another attempt for missed criteria, and discuss why receipt is not resolution. Record exercise completion only; it is not real operational qualification.
Validation:
The handoff contains SIM-042, 09:15 exercise time, Observe Queue, Needs review, and the observation that a placeholder monitoring update has not appeared on the practice display.
The participant identifies Practice Review Lead, states that the cause is unverified, and does not claim diagnosis or resolution.
The displayed status remains unchanged and no real message, access, or physical action occurs.
When the destination is absent, the participant pauses and asks the trainer instead of inventing a recipient.
The trainer observes each participant meeting every criterion; any missed criterion requires another attempt. Completion is for this fictional exercise only, not evidence of staff qualification.
Notes:
Simulation only: do not acknowledge, clear, change, or resolve alerts. No hardware manipulation, electrical work, privileged access, control bypass, diagnosis, or real escalation.
Stop if a real system, real operational detail, or an out-of-scope action is introduced; return to fictional materials.
Fictional fixture replay, not live AI generation. Human review against BOTH sources is required before export. This public guide is not approved operational instruction.
